01Goal

Build a watch-the-AI Pac-Man: a faithful neon-classic maze (per the reference above), four completely random ghosts, and a Pac-Man whose turning decisions are made only by the Laya decision model — the same convaiinnovations/laya checkpoint already installed on this machine — loaded in-process and running on the RTX 3050. The game is watched, not played: there is no keyboard control for Pac-Man.

Expect Laya to play imperfectly. A live test decision returned a flat distribution (up 0.35 / down 0.29 / left 0.19 / right 0.17) — coherent-ish, visibly indecisive. That is part of the show.

03Architecture

game loop (pygame)
   │  Pac-Man moves tile-by-tile every ~110 ms
   │  a decision is requested ONLY at junctions (≥2 legal moves, no reverse)
   ▼
laya_client.py ──── truncation guard · (state, legal) cache · loud errors
   ▼
laya.Agent(device="cuda")   ← loaded once at startup, warmup() run once
   ▼
local snapshot (offline, no Hub access)
  • No sidecar, no HTTP, no MCP in the game path — the game imports laya directly (one process, one command).
  • Junction-synchronous: the ~50–100 ms GPU call happens where it reads as a brief “thinking” micro-pause. Corridors, corners and straightaways cost zero model calls.
  • No fallbacks: if CUDA or the model is unavailable, the game raises with the exact fix. CPU play is explicitly out of scope.

04Game rules & mechanics

  • Maze: classic 28×31 properties — 4 power pellets in the corners, ghost house, side tunnels (edge wrap). No dead ends (guarantees a non-reverse move always exists).
  • Pacing: tile step 110 ms, multiplied by 0.95 per level, floor 70 ms.
  • Ghosts (random): 4 of them, classic colors, staggered house release; at each step a uniformly random legal neighbor, never reversing; they may use tunnels too.
  • Power pellets: all live ghosts reverse and turn frightened for 7 s (−0.5 s per level, floor 2 s); still random but edible. Blink during the last 2 s.
  • Eaten ghost → eyes: BFS shortest path back to the house, then respawn as a normal ghost (classic).
  • Lives: 3; contact with a deadly ghost resets positions (pellets stay eaten). Game over → press R.
  • Levels: clear all pellets → next level, speed-up, ghosts keep their behavior. Score: pellet 10, power pellet 50, ghost 200.
  • Keys: Esc quit · P pause · R restart.
  • HUD: classic layout — score on top, lives at the bottom.

05Laya interface

State sent (full maze, ~300–400 tokens)

############################
#o....G....#........#.....o#
#.###.###..#..####..#.###.#
#        … full 28×31 grid …        #
############################
legend: # wall   . pellet   o power pellet   ' ' empty
        P Pac-Man (facing left)   G deadly ghost
        f frightened ghost (edible)   E returning eyes (harmless)
legal moves: up, left

The decision call

  • Question: {"type":"choice","instructions":<legend + legal moves>,"criteria":{"up":"move up","down":"move down","left":"move left","right":"move right"}} — short labels only.
  • Post-filter the returned probabilities to the legal moves, then take the argmax. (The model can pick into a wall; the filter makes it impossible.)
  • Guards: raise if usage["truncated"] is set or options collapsed. Contract: the model must see the whole maze, every time.
  • Cache keyed by (grid_text, legal_moves) — identical junction states answer instantly after the first visit.
  • Log every decision: legal moves, probabilities, chosen move, latency.

06Rendering spec (neon)

100% procedural pygame — zero image assets. Constants for color/intensity are one-liners, easy to tune against the mockup.

  • Walls — classic double-line outline: one startup pass draws rounded blue segments on every wall-cell edge facing a corridor (no line between two wall cells). Bright mockup blue ≈ #1E6BFF.
  • Glow (baked bloom) — each element is rendered to its own surface, blurred by smoothscale down-4× → up, then additive-blitted (BLEND_ADD) under the sharp copy. Done once at startup for the maze and every sprite — zero per-frame cost. (Faithful vibe, not raytraced bloom.)
  • Pellets — small yellow squares with glow (as in the mockup, not dots); power pellets are large radial-gradient orbs, blinking.
  • Ghosts — classic dome + wavy skirt; red #FF0000, pink #FFB8FF, cyan #00FFFF, orange #FFB851; big white eyes with blue pupils offset toward travel direction; frightened variant (deep blue, white eyes); eyes-only variant. Glow baked per color.
  • Pac-Man — yellow disc, animated wedge mouth (3 frames), rotated per direction, glow baked.
  • Pre-rendered at init: Pac (4 directions × 3 mouth frames) · ghosts (4 colors × 4 directions + frightened + eyes).
  • Background: near-black. HUD bars black with the neon palette.

08Phase A — now (laptop on battery, no GPU)

Write & verify logic only
  1. Write maze.txt, game.py, laya_client.py, check.py.
  2. uv sync — installs pygame only (small download). No Laya, no torch, no GPU touched.
  3. uv run python check.py — 500-tick headless simulations, stub client, multiple seeds (assertions listed in §10).
  4. uv run python game.py --screenshot frame.png — render one styled frame and compare against the mockup; iterate glow, colors and sprite shapes until it matches.

No game is run; nothing touches the GPU. Everything above works today.

09Phase B — GPU day (plug in the charger first)

CUDA bring-up → live check → play
  1. Verify the dGPU re-enumerated (should return when on AC power): 
    powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-PnpDevice -Class Display | Select-Object Status,Problem,FriendlyName"
nvidia-smi
    Expect Status OK for “NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 6GB Laptop GPU” and a driver version from nvidia-smi. If it is still phantom on AC power: stop and reassess (Device Manager enable → driver reinstall). No CPU smuggling.
  2. Pick the CUDA line (cuXXX) matching the driver and available torch 2.14.1 builds; finalize [[tool.uv.index]] in pyproject.toml.
  3. uv sync --group gpu — downloads the CUDA torch build (~3 GB, one time).
  4. Verify torch sees the GPU: 
    uv run python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))"
  5. uv run python check.py --live — loads Laya on CUDA, makes one real junction decision, prints the distribution and latency (assertions in §10).
  6. uv run python game.py — play/watch. 🎮
The only hard dependency risk in this plan is step 1: if the RTX 3050 cannot be made active in Windows, CUDA is impossible and the project pauses there — the model runs on CPU only if you explicitly change your mind later.

10Verification & checks

Stub simulation — runs today, no model required

  • Pac-Man and ghosts never enter a wall; every move is from the legal set; no reversals.
  • Pellet count is monotonically non-increasing; clearing all pellets advances the level.
  • Power pellet → all ghosts reverse + become frightened; eating a frightened ghost scores and spawns eyes.
  • Eyes complete the BFS trip home and respawn normally.
  • Deadly contact decrements lives and resets positions; 0 lives → game over → R restarts.
  • Tunnel wrap works for both Pac-Man and ghosts (500 ticks × several seeds).

Live smoke — GPU day

  • Model loads on the expected device; warmup() completes.
  • One real junction state → exactly 4 option probabilities, sum ≈ 1.0, no truncated flag, no collapsed options; latency printed.

Visual QA

  • --screenshot frame vs the mockup: wall outline style, glow strength, pellet squares, ghost/Pac shapes, HUD placement.

11Risks & mitigations

RiskMitigation
dGPU stays phantom even on AC power (driver/BIOS problem)Stop; Device Manager enable → driver reinstall → reassess. Explicitly no CPU fallback.
Driver too old for the newest CUDA torch buildPick the older cu12x line that matches; update driver first if needed.
Full-maze state exceeds the prompt budgetGuarded by usage["truncated"]; levers: shorter legend, or raise max_len passed to predict().
Laptop thermals throttle the GPU during long sessionsPedestal/cooling; affects speed only, not correctness.
VRAM pressureModel is ~650 MB fp32 — comfortable in 6 GB VRAM.
